instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:3 the thoughts are to stay in sincere and pure devotion to Christ, from which deceit would lead them astray. In Heb 10:29 the hearers are asked to think of the one who profaned the blood by which he was sanctified.
observations.grounds: a sincere and pure devotion to Christ

observations.text: In 1Sa 20:3 David says Saul knows the favor he has with Jonathan and so thinks to keep it from him. In Pro 18:2 the fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in airing his opinion: his delight is in his own view. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought to give a pleasant land and be called Father.
observations.grounds: A fool takes no pleasure in understanding

observations.text: In 1Sa 27:11 David leaves none alive, thinking they would tell of him: the thought of a report drives the killing. In Ecc 9:10 there is no thought in Sheol, to which all are going: thought belongs to life. In Mat 18:12 leaving the ninety-nine is in the case the hearers are asked to think about.
observations.grounds: no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol

observations.text: In 1Sa 18:25 Saul says the king desires only a bride-price of foreskins, while he thinks to make David fall by the Philistines: the stated desire covers the thought. In 1Ch 28:9 Solomon is to serve with a willing mind, for the Lord understands every plan and thought. In 2Sa 14:17 and 2Ki 7:12 will is the future of the quoted thought.
observations.grounds: serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind

observations.text: In Psa 56:5 and Isa 59:7 the thoughts are of evil, with injury, desolation and destruction around them: the thoughts lead to harm. In Isa 10:7 the Assyrian's heart thinks to destroy. In 2Cor 10:5 the destroying is of arguments, and the thoughts are taken captive.
observations.grounds: it is in his heart to destroy

observations.text: Death is what the thought fears or expects in Gen 26:9 (Isaac thought he would die because of Rebekah), 1Sa 20:3 (a step between David and death), Job 29:18 (Job thought he would die in his nest) and Jon 1:6 (the captain hopes they will not perish). In Joh 11:13 they took Jesus' word of death for sleep, in Act 8:20 Simon's silver is to perish for his thought, and in 1Cor 4:9 Paul thinks the apostles are like men sentenced to death. In Judg 13:7 death goes with conceive in its bodily sense.
observations.grounds: I shall die in my nest

observations.text: In Jam 2:4 making distinctions among themselves is what shows them judges with evil thoughts: the favoring is the outward form of the thoughts.
observations.grounds: have you not then made distinctions among yourselves

observations.text: In Judg 13:3 barren is the woman's state before she is told she will conceive, in the bodily sense. In Luk 6:8 Jesus knows their thoughts and calls the man with the withered hand to stand: the withered hand is the occasion their thoughts watch.
observations.grounds: But he knew their thoughts

observations.text: In Job 20:2 Zophar's disquieting thoughts answer him because of the haste within him: the inner agitation drives the thoughts.
observations.grounds: because of my haste within me

observations.text: In Judg 13:3, Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 bear follows conceive in the bodily sense. In 2Ch 13:8 Abijah tells Jeroboam he thinks to withstand the Lord's kingdom: the thought is to resist. In Jer 40:5 and 1Cor 7:26 remain is what is judged good, and in 1Cor 4:9 Paul thinks the apostles are set last.
observations.grounds: you think to withstand the kingdom of the Lord

observations.text: In Gen 32:8 Jacob thinks that if Esau attacks one camp the other will escape: the thought plans an escape. In Est 4:13 Esther is not to think she will escape in the palace: the thought of escape is forbidden.
observations.grounds: the camp that is left will escape

observations.text: Evil is the content or the quality of the thoughts in Gen 6:5, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Psa 64:5, Isa 59:7, Jer 4:14, Eze 38:10, Mat 9:4, Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21 and Jam 2:4: the thoughts are evil, schemes to wrong, thoughts of iniquity that lodge within and come out of the heart. In Pro 12:5, Pro 15:26, Pro 21:29 and Isa 55:7 the wicked are set against the righteous and upright and are called to forsake their thoughts, and in Psa 10:4 the wicked man's thoughts deny God. In Job 15:35 evil is born of what is conceived, in 2Sa 14:17 the king discerns good and evil, and in 1Cor 14:20 the believers are to be infants in evil but mature in thinking.

observations.text: In 2Cor 9:5 Paul judged it needful to send the brothers on ahead: the judgment of what is needed leads to the urging.
observations.grounds: I thought it necessary to urge the brothers

observations.text: In Psa 73:16 when the psalmist thought how to understand the prosperity of the wicked, it was a wearisome task to him: the thinking wearies until he enters the sanctuary.
observations.grounds: it seemed to me a wearisome task

observations.text: In Jer 3:7 the Lord thought Israel would return, but she did not, and her treacherous sister saw it: the Lord's expectation is met by faithlessness.
observations.grounds: her treacherous sister Judah saw it

observations.text: In Psa 64:5 the wicked hold fast to their evil purpose and lay snares, thinking no one sees: the holding fast and the thought of being unseen go together.
observations.grounds: They hold fast to their evil purpose

observations.text: Fear and thought go together in Gen 20:11, Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, 2Sa 14:15 and Job 32:6: the person is afraid and the quoted thought gives the fear's reason (no fear of God here, you would take your daughters, the thing is known). In Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 the thoughts themselves alarm, and in Luk 24:37 the startled disciples think they see a spirit. In 2Cor 11:3 Paul is afraid for their thoughts.
observations.grounds: Because I was afraid, for I thought

observations.text: In Act 12:9 Peter follows the angel out, thinking he is seeing a vision: he acts while taking the real for a vision.
observations.grounds: thought he was seeing a vision

observations.text: In Pro 14:15 the simple believes everything while the prudent gives thought to his steps, and in Pro 18:2 the fool delights in airing his opinion. In Rom 1:21 futile thinking goes with foolish hearts darkened. In 1Cor 3:18 the one who thinks himself wise is to become a fool, and in 2Cor 11:16 and 2Cor 12:6 Paul weighs being thought a fool. Folly and right thought are set against each other.
observations.grounds: they became futile in their thinking

observations.text: In Jer 23:27 the prophets think to make the people forget the Lord's name by their dreams: the thought is a plan aimed at forgetting. In 2Pe 1:13 Peter thinks it right to stir them up by reminder: the judgment serves remembering.
observations.grounds: who think to make my people forget my name

observations.text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man who forsakes his thoughts and returns is promised abundant pardon: forsaking the thoughts is joined to God's pardon.
observations.grounds: for he will abundantly pardon

observations.text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man is to forsake his thoughts: the thoughts are what is to be left. In 1Ch 28:9 the Lord, who understands every plan and thought, will cast off the one who forsakes him.
observations.grounds: if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever

observations.text: In Mat 5:17 the hearers are not to think Jesus came to abolish the Law: the false thought is corrected by his coming to fulfill it.
observations.grounds: I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them

observations.text: In Joh 11:56 the people ask one another what they think, whether Jesus will come to the feast, and in Joh 13:29 some think Jesus sent Judas to buy for the feast: the feast is the setting of a view about Jesus, mistaken in Joh 13:29.
observations.grounds: Buy what we need for the feast

observations.text: In Phili 1:17 some proclaim Christ from selfish ambition, thinking to afflict Paul in prison: the intent to harm goes with the selfish motive.
observations.grounds: thinking to afflict me in my imprisonment

observations.text: In 2Ki 20:19 and Isa 39:8 Hezekiah thinks there will be peace and security in his days: the thought rests on his own safety. In 2Ch 32:1 Sennacherib besieges the walled towns, meaning to take them. In Jer 40:5 the captain of the guard leaves Jeremiah to go where he thinks right.
observations.grounds: There will be peace and security in my days

observations.text: In Mat 6:7 the Gentiles expect a hearing because they pile up words: a false view of prayer. observations.grounds: they think that they will be heard for their many words

observations.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

observations.text: In 1Ch 28:9, Psa 139:23 and Heb 4:12 the heart and the thoughts are searched and discerned together: the Lord tests every heart and grasps each plan, the psalmist asks God to know his heart and his thoughts, and the word discerns the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
observations.grounds: Search me, O God, and know my heart

observations.text: The mind is named as where thoughts come in Eze 11:5, Eze 20:32, Eze 38:10 and Dan 2:30: the things that come into the mind, what is in the mind, thoughts that come into the mind and the thoughts of the king's mind.
observations.grounds: thoughts will come into your mind

observations.text: In Rom 1:21 futile thinking goes with the foolish heart darkened, and in Jam 1:26 the one who thinks himself religious deceives his heart: the thinking and the state of the heart go together.
observations.grounds: deceives his heart

observations.text: In Jer 3:19 the Lord's thought is of giving Israel a heritage most beautiful and being called Father: the heritage is the gift the thought intended.
observations.grounds: a heritage most beautiful of all nations

observations.text: In 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3 the princes ask Hanun whether he thinks David is honoring his father: the thought about honor is turned to suspicion. observations.text: In Joh 5:45 the hearers are not to think Jesus will accuse them, for Moses, in whom they hope, does: the false thought is set against where their hope lies. In Job 6:26 Job asks if they think to reprove the words of a despairing man.
observations.grounds: Moses, on whom you have set your hope

observations.text: In Isa 59:7 the feet that are swift to shed innocent blood belong to those whose thoughts are thoughts of iniquity: the act and the thoughts are named together.
observations.grounds: swift to shed innocent blood

observations.text: Intention and thought stand side by side in Gen 6:5, 1Ch 28:9 and 1Ch 29:18, where the same pair of words names the formed purpose and the thoughts of the heart; in Psa 64:5 the evil purpose goes with the quoted thought, and in Isa 10:7 the Assyrian does not so intend nor his heart so think.
